**Section:** Jātaka (ja)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Lābhagarahajātaka* (Ja 287) is a story in the Pali Jātaka collection, positioned within the *Abbhantaravagga* [Fausböll 1879]. According to its commentary, the Buddha delivered the narrative while residing at Jetavana concerning a fellow monk or co-resident (*saddhivihārika*) of Venerable Sāriputta [SuttaCentral; Fausböll 1879]. The verse narrative opens with the words *Nānummatto ti* [SuttaCentral; Fausböll 1879]. In the story of the past, the Bodhisatta was a world-renowned teacher (*ācariya* / *disāpāmokkha*), while the young pupil (*māṇava*) who praised renunciation and went forth as a hermit (*isipabbajjā*) to attain the Brahma realm was the former incarnation of the gain-condemning monk [Fausböll 1879; Luce et al. 1970].

Depictions of the story survive in the epigraphy and art of early Pagan (Burma), where corridor wall painting glosses identify the Bodhisatta of the *lābhagaraha jāt* as a *disāpāmokkha* [Luce et al. 1970].

According to SuttaCentral, passage-level parallels exist in other Jātaka tales, including the *Chavakajātaka* (Ja 309), *Seyyajātaka* (Ja 310), and *Lomasakassapajātaka* (Ja 433), as well as the Vinaya *Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga* (Sekhiya 69) [SuttaCentral]. Automated text-reuse analysis in DharmaNexus identifies ten Pali-internal reuse passages shared with two sections of the *Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā* (Dutiyo bhāgo and Tatiyo bhāgo), particularly covering segments 2.1–3.4, while recording no cross-language parallels meeting threshold criteria [DharmaNexus].
